# omada_dns_proxy (Resource)

Manages the site's DNS proxy and DNS-over-HTTPS resolvers.

This is a singleton per site — import it with the site name rather than creating it.

~> **This decides who sees every DNS query the network makes.** DoH stops your ISP and anyone on the path from reading them — and hands that same visibility to whoever runs the resolver you point at. Choosing a resolver is choosing who to trust with that log, so prefer one whose retention policy you have actually read, or run your own.

The controller keeps two server lists and they are **not** the same kind of thing. `enabled_default_server_types` selects from a fixed list built into the firmware, which this resource never rewrites — see `available_default_servers` for what it offers. `custom_server` blocks are yours and are managed in full.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# DNS proxy with a customised DNS-over-HTTPS resolver.
#
# Whoever runs the resolver you point at sees every query the network makes, so
# this is a trust decision as much as a configuration one.
resource "omada_dns_proxy" "this" {
  enable = true

  # Select from the firmware's built-in resolvers by `type`. Read the available
  # values from this resource's own `available_default_servers` output.
  enabled_default_server_types = []

  custom_server {
    name = "hagezi"
    urls = ["https://root.hagezi.org/dns-query"]
  }
}

output "builtin_doh_resolvers" {
  value = omada_dns_proxy.this.available_default_servers
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `custom_server` (Block List) A customised DoH resolver. Declared in order; the controller stores the list as given. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--custom_server))
- `enable` (Boolean) Whether the gateway's DNS proxy is active. With this off, the resolver lists below have no effect.
- `enabled_default_server_types` (List of Number) Controller `type` values of the firmware-provided DoH resolvers to enable. The list of available types is fixed by the firmware and reported in `available_default_servers`; a type that is not in it is an error, because the controller would accept the write and silently drop it.
- `site` (String) Site name. Defaults to the primary site. Changing forces replacement.

### Read-Only

- `available_default_servers` (Attributes List) The firmware's DoH resolvers as the controller reports them. Read-only; use it to find the `type` values for `enabled_default_server_types`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--available_default_servers))
- `doh_server_limit` (Number) Maximum customised DoH servers this controller accepts. Read-only.
- `dot_server_limit` (Number) Maximum DNS-over-TLS servers. Read-only — DoT itself has no endpoint on this firmware.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `site_id` (String)
- `supports_dns_override` (Boolean) Whether the gateway can override client-specified DNS. Read-only.

<a id="nestedblock--custom_server"></a>
### Nested Schema for `custom_server`

Required:

- `name` (String) Label for this resolver.
- `urls` (List of String) DoH endpoint URLs, e.g. `https://root.hagezi.org/dns-query`. May not be empty.

Optional:

- `enable` (Boolean) Whether this resolver is used.


<a id="nestedatt--available_default_servers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `available_default_servers`

Read-Only:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether it is currently on.
- `type` (Number) Controller enum identifying the resolver.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Singleton per site — import by site name.
terraform import omada_dns_proxy.this Default
```
